_comment: RTC require-auth contract, governed by ADR-0101 (tina4-python#252).
The /api/rtc/config route mints a fresh TURN credential on every call and the
/ws/rtc/{room} signalling socket relays a call. Left public, anyone can use the
operator's TURN server as a relay. Both are secured by DEFAULT; an app that
genuinely wants anonymous calling opts out with TINA4_RTC_REQUIRE_AUTH=false.
Secure-by-default: only an explicit false/0/no/off opens them - any other value
(or unset) keeps them secured. The same six cases run in all four frameworks on
a real realtime()/mount() registration, no mocks: auth_required is read straight
off the registered route (HTTP route table + WebSocket route table).
feature: RTC config + signalling require auth by default (tina4-python#252)

invariants.rule: With no TINA4_RTC_REQUIRE_AUTH set, both the /api/rtc/config route and the /ws/rtc/{room} signalling socket require a valid token (auth_required true).
invariants.why: The config route mints a TURN credential on every call and the signalling socket relays a call; public, they let anyone use the operator's TURN server as a relay, and a short credential TTL does not bound the abuse. Security-by-default (tina4-python#252).
cases: config route requires auth by default
signalling socket requires auth by default
require auth explicit true secures both

invariants.rule: TINA4_RTC_REQUIRE_AUTH=false (or 0/no/off) makes both the config route and the signalling socket public again, for apps that want anonymous calling.
invariants.why: Anonymous calling is a real use case (the browser needs ICE before it can authenticate anywhere); the operator opts into the exposure explicitly rather than having it by default.
cases: require auth false opens the config route
require auth false opens the signalling socket

invariants.rule: Only an explicit false/0/no/off opts out; any other value (or unset) keeps the routes secured, so a typo never silently opens the TURN relay.
invariants.why: A whitelist-truthy parse would treat an unrecognised value as 'not true' and open the relay; secure-by-default requires the opposite - open only on a recognised opt-out.
cases: only explicit falsey opens the route
